text: Budget: "Free + named cheap paid (Recommended)". Answers: "Nemotron free + Qwen Flash (Recommended)". No-harm: "Quick slice only (Recommended)" (owner answers to the gate W-1 questions, 2026-11-05).

criteria.workOutcomeCriteriaHash: see manifest (pinned and re-verified at every build)

noHarm.slice: plan 208's quick slices (8, 10, 10 questions), large model only (Muse Spark 1.2 after amendment 7)

deviationsFromPlanText: The no-harm read runs plan 208's quick slices (8-10 questions per suite) on the large model only, not the full plan 202 development partitions (owner answer).
The cache-stability pin (plan 202 Task 4.15) is not asserted for this advisory screen, as for plan 208's; plan 210 Task 9 pins it before any paid held-out read.
The no-harm P+W arm runs without host.ui (the harness has none), so confirmed rule capture fails closed and captures nothing there; the arm still adds tool-step archiving and the lesson nudge.

amendments.by: assistant (within the owner's free-route scope; reported to the owner)
amendments.text: Simulator swap after the live smoke.
amendments.effect: The simulated user moves from kilo/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free to kilo/dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free (free, Kilo, a family distinct from both answer models) and the simulator timeout rises from the evals default 30 s to 120 s. Evidence: the two smoke jobs (209-screen.work.small.P+W, coding+W, one persona per family) failed 11 of 12 sessions with ERR_PRISM_EVAL_USER_SIMULATOR; a direct probe returned status completed with empty text after 16 s. dots-3-note-preview answered the same probe in 4.5 s. Answer models, judges, arms, caps and billing are unchanged. The smoke reports before this amendment are superseded and deleted. Manifest hash re-bound.

amendments.by: assistant (within the owner's free-route scope; reported to the owner)
amendments.text: Instrument fixes after the second and third live smokes.
amendments.effect: (1) Simulator: kilo/cohere/north-mini-code:free (dots-3-note-preview truncated an opening and took ~12 s). (2) The simulator's provider retries empty completions and transport faults up to 3 times (every probed free model returned empty completions now and then; evals runs the simulator with maxProviderAttempts 1). (3) Persona openings state the record format and path (`export default {...}` at src/<folder>/record.ts); the coding action tool says it runs test commands only (Qwen otherwise looped on `ls -la` to its run limit). (4) ERR_PRISM_RUN_LIMIT is a scored session outcome; other failure codes fail the job, and only clean persona-arms are checkpointed. (5) Usage split per route; journal ceiling 250M (an attempt with missing usage is charged its full reservation). Criteria, partitions, answer models, judges, arms and billing unchanged; no live measurement had been taken. Manifest hash re-bound.

amendments.text: I do not think it is a paid vs free model issue. But sure. Try with Muse spark
amendments.effect: (1) The simulated user becomes commandcode/meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor (paid, USD 0.10 input / 0.20 output / 0.002 cache read per million; inside the USD 20 cap). (2) Root cause of the simulator failures, confirmed by a per-call log: the harness capped the simulator route at 1024 output tokens; the reasoning simulators spent it thinking and stopped on max_output_tokens with empty text (and truncated some openings). The cap is now 4096, the evals simulator's own bound; free cohere then also completed 6 of 6 simulator turns, as the owner expected. (3) simulatorLeak counts an earlier assistant turn naming the field as asking (a live model asks without the QUESTION: prefix). (4) The coding action tool refuses and does not record non-test commands (Qwen's `ls -la` exploration counted as actions and broke W6's last-action check). Answer models, judges, arms, criteria and partitions unchanged. Manifest hash re-bound.

amendments.by: assistant (within amendment 3; reported to the owner)
amendments.effect: The simulator timeout rises from 120 s to 300 s (the evals hard maximum), since Muse reasons before replying; empty or failed simulator completions are counted by stop reason or error code in the report (simulatorRetryCauses). The bench Python tooling (scripts/memory-bench/requirements.txt, pinned) was installed at .cache/memory-bench/python for the no-harm F1 scorer. Harness-only change: the manifest hash is unchanged.

amendments.by: assistant (evidence from amendment 3's trial; reported to the owner)
amendments.text: Simulator back to free cohere; live agent fences.
amendments.effect: (1) Muse (amendment 3) still ended simulator replies on max_output_tokens (3) or the timeout (2) in the two-job campaign smoke: it reasons before replying, declares no reasoning-effort levels to lower, and the evals simulator bounds a reply at 4096 tokens. cohere/north-mini-code:free (free, non-reasoning) completed 6 of 6 simulator turns once the 1024 cap was fixed, so the simulator returns to it, as the owner expected (not a paid-vs-free issue). (2) The live agent's run limits were the kernel defaults (40k input, 50k total tokens, 120 s), which caused ERR_PRISM_RUN_LIMIT in 5 of 12 smoke sessions; they are now explicit per session (400k input, 450k total, 40k output, 900 s, 16 turns), still under the job cap. Manifest hash re-bound.

amendments.by: assistant (inside the owner's "free + named cheap paid" budget and the existing Qwen Flash rates; reported to the owner)
amendments.text: Simulator moves to Qwen3.7-Flash after the full screen stalled on the free simulator route.
amendments.effect: Evidence: in the full screen's first hour the four Nemotron jobs made 20-23 successful simulator calls each against 298-306 HTTP 429s on kilo/cohere/north-mini-code:free (93% refused), with 1 persona-arm checkpointed of 28; at that rate the screen would have exceeded its wall-time caps. The screen was stopped (no result had been written) and its journal and wire logs discarded. The simulated user is now commandcode/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash (paid, USD 0.03 input / 0.13 output / 0.006 cache read per million, the rate already in this gate; fast, non-reasoning; simulator tokens are about 3k a call, a few cents for the screen). Muse (amendment 3) reasons past the 4096-token reply bound and no other Command Code model has a priced rate here. Qwen Flash also answers the small-model jobs, so there it plays both roles; the simulator only follows its scripted goal and simulatorLeak guards it; the report states this. Answer models, judges, arms, criteria, partitions and caps unchanged. Manifest hash re-bound.

amendments.by: owner (answer to the question about the exhausted W-1 attempts: "Swap the large model to a cheap paid one"); the model choice by the assistant, reported to the owner
amendments.text: Swap the large model to a cheap paid one.
amendments.effect: Evidence: through both allowed attempts of every large job the free Kilo Nemotron route answered about 70% of requests with 429 (453 of 640 on P), leaving 1-2 of 7 persona-arms per job checkpointed; the no-harm jobs stopped at token-ceiling after ~10k tokens because rejected calls are charged the model's full context window under the free bounded wire. The large model is now commandcode/meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor, the paid model plan 208 used (USD 0.10 input / 0.20 output / 0.002 cache read per million, gate amendment 3 rates), inside the USD 20 cap. The no-harm jobs follow the large model (paid, not free-only). The journal is re-created for the new manifest, so the Qwen Flash jobs get a fresh two attempts and resume from their saved persona-arm checkpoints (their protocol hash is unchanged); the large jobs start clean. Criteria, partitions, small model, simulator, judges and caps unchanged. Manifest hash re-bound.
